extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative standards for suspending/deferring action, terminating suspensions, and computing/handling statutory and shortened reply periods in U.S. patent prosecution (MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of suspension request on CPA processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspension request acts to suspend a first Office action by the examiner but will not affect the processing of the CPA for a missing part. The applicant will be given a notice that provides a time period of 2 months from the date of the notification to pay the CPA basic filing fee, the search fee, the examination fee, and the surcharge set forth in 37 CFR 1.16(f). Applicant must pay the CPA basic filing fee, the search fee, the examination fee, and the surcharge within 2 months to avoid the abandonment of the CPA. Pursuant to applicant’s request for suspension, the action by the Office will be suspended on the CPA for the period requested by the applicant, starting on the filing date of the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the CPA and suspension request are proper, the Office will suspend action on the CPA starting from the CPA filing date. Payment within two months is mandatory to avoid abandonment. If the CPA has missing parts, processing of the CPA (e.g., requirement to supply missing parts) continues even though the first Office action is suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE or CPA (no filing date granted)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CPA or the RCE is improper (e.g., a filing date was not accorded in the CPA or the RCE was filed without a submission or the RCE fee), the Office will not recognize the request for suspension, and action by the Office will not be suspended. A notice of improper CPA or RCE will be sent to applicant as appropriate. The time period set in the previous Office communication continues to run from the mailing date of that communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure a filing date is accorded and required fees/submissions accompany an RCE/CPA. If corrected later, the request for suspension should be resubmitted; the request will not be processed until the Office accords a filing date or receives a proper RCE in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper request for suspension—timeliness and fee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CPA or the RCE is properly filed, but the request for suspension is improper (e.g., the request for suspension was filed untimely or without the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i)), action by the Office will not be suspended on the application. The Office will process the CPA or RCE and place the application on the examiner’s docket. The examiner will notify the applicant of the denial of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph ¶7.56.01 to deny improper requests for suspension; in the form, insert the filing date of the request. Ensure suspension requests are filed timely and accompanied by the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for deferral of examination—basic rule and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In new applications, applicants may request a deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) for a period not extending beyond three years from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is claimed. The request must be filed before the Office issues an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance. The suspension will start on the day that the Office grants the request for deferral of examination. Once the deferral of examination has been granted, the application will not be taken up for action by the examiner until the suspension period expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral cannot extend beyond 3 years from earliest effective filing date. Example: a maximum allowed deferral results in action being suspended until the computed date (example given: foreign priority 1/3/00 leads to resumption on 1/4/03). The request must be granted by the Office before suspension begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required for a request for deferral (Form PTO/SB/37)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for deferral of examination under 37 CFR 1.103(d) must include: (A) a period of suspension, in a whole number of months, not extending beyond three years from the earliest effective filing date; (B) the publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d); and (C) the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no period of suspension is included or a period exceeding the maximum is included, the Office will assume the maximum period (3 years) is requested. Form PTO/SB/37 may be used to submit the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility conditions for granting deferral of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not grant a deferral of examination unless the following conditions are met: (A) the application must be (1) an original utility or plant application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or (2) an application resulting from entry of an international application into the national stage after compliance with 37 CFR 1.495 (cannot be a design application, reissue application, or CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d)); (B) the application must be filed on or after November 29, 2000; (C) the applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under 37 CFR 1.213(a), or if such a request was filed, the applicant must file a request under 37 CFR 1.213(b) to rescind it; (D) the application must be in condition for publication as provided in 37 CFR 1.211(c); and (E) the Office has not issued an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All five conditions are cumulative. If any condition is not met (e.g., application is a design or reissue, or a first Office action has been issued), deferral must be denied. See MPEP for more detail on the publication condition and rescinding nonpublication requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper request for deferral—denial form and reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request is improper, use form paragraph ¶7.56.02 to notify the applicant of denial. The notice should insert the filing date of the request and the reason(s) for denying the request (e.g., applicant did not rescind a nonpublication request, a first Office action has been issued, applicant has not submitted a request for voluntary publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In the form, insert the filing date and specific reason(s) for denial. See MPEP §709 for examples of appropriate reasons to insert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of proper request for deferral—supervisory approval required
rubrics_metrics.description: A supervisory patent examiner’s approval is required for the grant of a deferral of examination in an application. If the request is proper, use form paragraph ¶7.54.01 to notify applicant that the request has been approved and indicate the number of months for the deferral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: Insert the filing date of the request and the number of months for the deferral in the form paragraph. Supervisory approval must be obtained before granting deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of suspension of action—applicant-initiated
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit a request for termination of the suspension of action prior to the end of the suspension period. The request for termination is effective when an appropriate official of the Office takes action thereon. If the request properly identifies the application and the period of suspension has not expired when the Office acts on the request, the Office will terminate the suspension and place the application on the examiner’s docket. An acknowledgment should be sent using form ¶7.54.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include filing date of the request in the acknowledgment form. Termination becomes effective on the date of mailing the notice of approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-initiated suspension—limits and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action at the initiative of the Office should be avoided when possible because it causes delays and may affect patent term. Every Office-initiated suspension will be limited to a time period of a maximum of 6 months. An examiner may grant an initial suspension on his or her own initiative for a maximum of 6 months. A second or subsequent suspension requires the TC Director’s approval (see MPEP §1003) and the notification for any second/subsequent suspension must be signed by the TC Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the suspension reason no longer exists, terminate the suspension immediately even if the suspension period has not expired. For continuing problems (e.g., reference still unavailable), the examiner should try other sources or update the search before seeking another suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(f)—decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(f) is decided by the Technology Center (TC) Director of work group 3640.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer contested or complex requests under paragraph (f) to the named TC Director for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs for Office-initiated suspensions (awaiting reference, interference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ¶7.52 for 'Suspension of Action, Awaiting New Reference' and ¶7.53 for 'Suspension of Action, Possible Interference', each specifying 'SUSPENDED FOR A PERIOD OF [1] MONTHS from the mailing date of this letter.' The examiner note states maximum period for suspension is six months and that the TC Director must approve all second or subsequent suspensions, with the TC Director’s signature on second/subsequent suspension letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the suspension period in bracket [1]. For second or subsequent suspensions, obtain TC Director approval and signature. Upon expiration, applicant should be invited to inquire as to status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping applications by same applicant—handling when related to an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should not consider ex parte questions which are pending before the Office in inter partes proceedings involving the same applicant. The better practice is to reject claims in an application related to another application in interference over the counts of the interference and, if such claims are not canceled in the outside application, suspend prosecution of the outside application pending final determination of priority in the interference. If the applicant wishes to prosecute the outside application and presents good reasons, prosecution should be continued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When related claims are at issue in an interference, prefer rejection over consideration ex parte. If applicant shows good cause to proceed, follow precedent (e.g., Ex parte Bullier, In re Seebach, In re Hammell) and MPEP §2300 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory period for reply—35 U.S.C. 133 and 37 CFR 1.135
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time period provided under §1.134 and §1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise. The maximum statutory period for reply to an Office action is 6 months (35 U.S.C. 133). Shortened periods are commonly used. 37 CFR 1.135(b) specifies that admission of (or refusal to admit) any amendment after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not operate to save the application from abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply must be a complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require to avoid abandonment. Be aware amendments after final action or non-responsive amendments do not save the application under 1.135(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona fide attempt to reply and inadvertent omissions—37 CFR 1.135(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply by the applicant is a bona fide attempt to advance the application and is substantially a complete reply but for an inadvertent omission, applicant may be given a shortened statutory time period (generally 1 month) to supply the omission. If the omission precludes action on the merits (e.g., unsigned amendment, missing fees), the examiner may consider the reply adequate to avoid abandonment and give a 1-month period to correct; failure to timely supply the omission results in abandonment. If the omission does not preclude action on the merits (e.g., reply fails to address a rejection), the examiner may waive the deficiency and act on the application or require correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether to provide a 1-month shortened statutory period is within examiner discretion. If the examiner determines the omission was not inadvertent or is being abused to delay, do not grant the shortened period; instead require the omission be supplied within the original period for reply. See MPEP §714.03 for abuse examples and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of the statutory period for reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual time taken for reply is computed from the date stamped or printed on the Office action to the date of receipt by the Office of applicant’s reply. No fractions of a day are taken; the reply is due on the corresponding day of the month '6 months' (or other number) after the Office action. Examples: reply to an action dated Nov 30 with 3-month shortened period is due on Feb 28 (or 29); action dated Feb 28 is due on May 28. A 1-month extension shifts the due date to the corresponding day in the next month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing periods that end on months with fewer days (e.g., Jan 31 to Apr 30), follow the provided examples. When a timely reply is not filed, the application is regarded as abandoned after midnight of the date the period expired. Indicate explicit expiration dates when extensions are by irregular amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.136 allows an applicant to extend a nonstatutory or shortened statutory time period up to the earlier of the expiration of any maximum period set by statute or five months after the time period set for reply, by filing a petition and the fee set in §1.17(a), unless exceptions apply. If paragraph (a) provisions are not available, paragraph (b) permits extension for sufficient cause only if filed on or before the day the reply is due and accompanied by the petition fee set forth in §1.17(g). Certain time periods set in a 'Notice of Allowability' (e.g., oath under §1.63, formal drawings under §1.85(c), deposit under §1.809(c)) are not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions to extensions under paragraph (a) include reply briefs under §41.41, requests for oral hearing under §41.47(a), replies to Board decisions, and contests. Constructive petitions and fee submissions may be treated as petitions for extension for concurrent/future replies. See cross-references (§1.304, §1.550(c), §1.956) for other proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory periods—typical lengths and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period may not be less than 30 days. Typical shortened statutory periods used include: 1 month (not less than 30 days) for requirement for restriction/election of species only or to correct inadvertent omission in a bona fide reply (MPEP §710.01 and §714.03); 2 months for e.g. winning party in terminated interference to reply to an unanswered Office action or to reply to an Ex parte Quayle action; 3 months to reply to any Office action on the merits. Periods vary by situation and may be changed under rare circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate a shortened time prominently on the first page of actions. Shortened periods are subject to 37 CFR 1.136 unless otherwise notified. Use the MPEP-listed typical periods as starting points (1, 2, 3 months) and adjust only where justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restarting the reply period for defective Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the citation of a reference is incorrect or an Office action contains some other defect and this error is called to the attention of the Office within 1 month of the mail date of the action, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected, if requested to do so by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must call defects to the Office’s attention within one month of mailing to request restarting the period. Examiners should correct defects promptly and reset periods as appropriate per MPEP §710.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified time limits—situations and non-abandonment consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain situations use specified time limits (which are not shortened statutory periods) where failure to act results in consequences other than abandonment. Examples: (A) where a public petition for access is filed, applicant may get a specified time (usually 3 weeks) to state objections — failure does not affect prosecution but Office decides without applicant input; (B) an IDS missing some content may be given 1 month to complete the IDS — failure places noncomplying information in the file but not considered; (C) where an application is otherwise allowable but contains a traverse of a restriction requirement, applicant may be given a specified time (e.g., 1 month) to cancel nonelected claims — failure is treated as authorization to cancel and application passed to issue; (D) an examiner may require adding a claim to provoke an interference and set a time (not less than 1 month) — failure operates as concession of priority for the claim subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified time limits may be shorter than 30 days and do not cause abandonment if missed; consequences vary (loss of right regarding the particular matter, nonconsideration, cancellation, concession of priority). Examiners should state whether 37 CFR 1.136 extensions do not apply when setting such limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between shortened statutory periods and specified time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortened statutory periods (under 35 U.S.C. 133) and specified time limits differ: (A) failure to meet a specified time affects rights only as to that particular matter, whereas failure to meet a statutory period results in abandonment of the entire application; (B) a specified time limit may be set to less than the 30-day statutory minimum, unlike a shortened statutory period; (C) examiners may excuse a day or two late for specified time limits at their discretion, but any late reply to a shortened statutory period results in abandonment (though extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 may be available where permitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When setting specified time limits, indicate whether extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 apply. Be cautious: a one-day delay under a statutory shortened period is fatal to prosecution unless proper extension/petition procedures were available and complied with.
